summary: God asks for willingly given materials and directs the making of a sanctuary in which to dwell among Israel. Instructions specify the covenant ark with its gold cover and cherubim, the table with the bread of the presence, and a branching gold lamp stand, all according to the pattern shown to Moses.
whyItMatters: The detailed objects serve the stated purpose of divine presence among the people. Their materials, carrying poles, and placement distinguish a portable covenant sanctuary from an undefined collection of precious decorations.

context.author: Exodus does not name its final author. It records Moses writing particular covenant material; traditional Mosaic attribution and modern accounts of composition are distinguished in the book briefing.
context.audience: Israel remembering its rescue from Egypt and its obligations as a covenant community. The chapter does not identify an individual dedicatee.
context.date: The narrative places these events at Sinai after the departure from Egypt. The date of the events and the history of the book’s composition are separate, debated questions.
context.setting: God's speech to Moses on Mount Sinai, describing furnishings for the future sanctuary in Israel's camp.
context.literaryForm: A contribution appeal followed by architectural and craft specifications for three principal furnishings.

before.text: Moses has entered the cloud on Sinai for a prolonged stay after the covenant ceremony. The sanctuary instructions are given within that mountain encounter.

here.text: The purpose of dwelling among Israel introduces instructions for the ark, table, and lamp stand, with the shown pattern controlling the work.

after.text: The next chapter describes the fabric coverings, wooden frame, veil, and entrance that will house and separate these furnishings.

outline.heading: Willing contributions and a dwelling
outline.note: Materials are requested from willing hearts for a sanctuary made to the shown pattern.

outline.heading: The ark and its carrying poles
outline.note: A gold-covered wooden chest will hold the covenant.

outline.heading: The gold cover and cherubim
outline.note: God promises to meet and speak from above the covered ark.

outline.heading: The table and bread of the presence
outline.note: A gold-covered table, carrying apparatus, and vessels support the continual bread.

outline.heading: The branching gold lamp stand
outline.note: One hammered work with almond-flower forms carries seven lamps and follows the mountain pattern.

keyVerses.text: Let them make me a sanctuary, that I may dwell among them.
keyVerses.why: The chapter states the purpose of the sanctuary directly: God will dwell among the people.

keyVerses.text: There I will meet with you, and I will tell you from above the mercy seat, from between the two cherubim which are on the ark of the covenant, all that I command you for the children of Israel.
keyVerses.why: The ark is associated with divine meeting and instruction for Israel.

keyVerses.text: See that you make them after their pattern, which has been shown to you on the mountain.
keyVerses.why: The final command returns to the shown pattern as the standard for the work.

questions.question: Are the contributions described as a fixed tax?
questions.answer: The opening asks for offerings from everyone whose heart makes them willing and lists the materials needed. No uniform amount or payment rate is set in this chapter's contribution appeal.

questions.question: What is the stated reason for building the sanctuary?
questions.answer: God says it is so that he may dwell among them. That purpose connects the following objects and measurements to the life of the whole community.

questions.question: What is the “ark” here?
questions.answer: It is a rectangular acacia-wood chest overlaid with gold, fitted with rings and permanent carrying poles, and intended to hold the covenant. The word refers to a chest here, rather than a boat.

questions.question: What does the “mercy seat” refer to physically?
questions.answer: In this edition it is the pure-gold cover placed on top of the ark, made with two cherubim at its ends. The chapter associates the space above it with God's meeting and speech; it does not describe an ordinary chair for a human occupant.

questions.question: Does the chapter explain what every cherub feature symbolizes?
questions.answer: It specifies their wings, faces, location, and construction as one piece with the cover. The figures face each other and the cover, framing the place from which God promises to speak. A symbolic explanation of each feature is not supplied.

questions.question: What distinguishes the table from the ark?
questions.answer: The table carries dishes and other gold vessels and is to have the bread of the presence before God always. Like the ark it has rings and poles for movement, but it serves a different stated purpose and has different dimensions.

questions.question: How are the lamp stand’s unity and branches described?
questions.answer: It is one hammered work with a central shaft and six side branches, ornamented with cups, buds, and almond blossoms. Seven lamps illuminate the space in front, while the final command again requires the pattern shown on the mountain.

glossary.def: The gold-covered wooden chest intended to contain the covenant and carried by poles.
The winged figures made at the ends of the ark’s gold cover, facing inward.
Bread placed continually on the table before God.
